learn: The beat is the steady pulse that runs through music.
When you tap your foot to a song, you are finding the beat.
Some beats are strong and some are weak. In a march, the pattern is STRONG, weak, STRONG, weak.
check: Tapping your foot to a song finds the...
In a march, the pattern is...
lessons.try: March to a song and stomp on the strong beats.

learn: Beats are grouped into sets called measures.
Music in 2 has a strong beat then one weak beat. Music in 3 has a strong beat then two weak beats, like a waltz: ONE, two, three.
Bar lines separate measures in written music.
check: What separates measures in written music?
lessons.try: Pat your knees on ONE and clap on two, three to a waltz.

learn: When musicians play together, everyone follows the same beat.
A conductor or drummer can lead the beat.
If you get lost, listen and find the beat again.
check: When musicians play together, they follow...
lessons.try: Play a beat with a family member and try to stay perfectly together.

learn: A quarter note (ta) lasts one beat. Two eighth notes (ti-ti) share one beat.
A half note (ta-a) lasts two beats. It has an open head and a stem.
A whole note (ta-a-a-a) lasts four beats.
check: How many beats is a half note?
How many beats is a whole note?
lessons.try: Clap: ta, ta, ta-a. Then: ti-ti, ti-ti, ta-a-a-a.

learn: Rests are silent beats.
A quarter rest is one beat of silence. A half rest is two beats.
Count rests in your head so you come back in on time.
check: A half rest is how many beats of silence?
What do you do during a rest?
To come back in on time
lessons.try: Clap "ta, rest, ti-ti, ta" four times.

learn: You can write rhythms in a four-beat measure.
Each measure must add up to four beats: ta, ta, ti-ti, ta = 4.
Read your rhythm, then clap it.
check: In a four-beat measure, ta + ta + ta-a equals...
Ta, ti-ti, ta, ta is how many beats?
lessons.try: Write four measures of rhythm and have someone clap them.

learn: Pitch is how high or low a note is.
Music is written on a staff of five lines and four spaces.
Higher notes sit higher on the staff.
check: How many lines are on a staff?
How high or low a note is
lessons.try: Draw a staff and place three notes going up.

learn: Solfege gives names to pitches: do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti, do.
Many songs use do, re, mi, sol and la. This five-note set is called pentatonic.
Hand signs show each pitch.
check: The five notes do, re, mi, sol, la make a...
lessons.try: Sing do, re, mi, sol, la up and down.

learn: Melodies move up, down or stay the same.
Steps move to the next note. Skips jump over a note. Leaps jump far.
"Hot Cross Buns" moves down by step: mi, re, do.
check: Moving to the next note is a...
lessons.try: Sing "Hot Cross Buns" and show the steps with your hands.

learn: pp means pianissimo, very soft. p means piano, soft.
mp means mezzo piano, medium soft. mf means mezzo forte, medium loud.
f means forte, loud. ff means fortissimo, very loud.
lessons.try: Say your name at each dynamic level, from pp to ff.

learn: A crescendo sign looks like an opening angle: <. It means get louder.
A decrescendo sign looks like a closing angle: >. It means get softer.
Smooth changes make music expressive.
lessons.try: Hum one long note doing a crescendo then a decrescendo.

learn: Composers choose dynamics to create a mood.
In Grieg's "In the Hall of the Mountain King" (1875), the music starts very soft and gets louder and faster to an exciting end.
Listen for dynamic changes in music you hear.
check: How does "In the Hall of the Mountain King" start?
lessons.try: Listen to "In the Hall of the Mountain King" and raise your hand slowly as it gets louder.

learn: Your chest voice is lower, like your speaking voice.
Your head voice is higher and lighter, like a gentle owl hoot.
Good singers use both and move smoothly between them.
check: Sliding like a siren helps you...
lessons.try: Slide from a low "ooh" to a high "ooh" like a siren.

learn: Stand tall with feet apart, knees loose and shoulders relaxed.
Breathe low into your belly. Your shoulders stay still.
Use your breath to hold long notes steady.
lessons.try: Hold a note for as long as you can while standing tall.

learn: Singing in unison means everyone sings the same notes together.
A round is when groups sing the same song but start at different times, like "Row, Row, Row Your Boat".
Listen to blend with others, not to be the loudest.
check: When singing in a group, you should...
lessons.try: Sing "Row, Row, Row Your Boat" as a round with your family.

learn: String instruments vibrate strings: violin, viola, cello, double bass, harp, guitar.
Woodwinds use air: flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon, saxophone.
The bassoon is a big, low woodwind.
check: The biggest string instrument in the orchestra is the...
lessons.try: Listen to a flute and a bassoon. Describe their sounds.

learn: Brass players buzz their lips: trumpet, French horn, trombone, tuba.
The trombone has a slide that changes pitch.
Percussion is struck or shaken. Pitched percussion, like the xylophone, plays melodies. Unpitched, like a snare drum, plays rhythms.
check: Which brass instrument has a slide?
lessons.try: Name one pitched and one unpitched percussion instrument.

learn: An orchestra seats instruments in sections, with strings at the front.
Prokofiev's "Peter and the Wolf" (1936) gives each character an instrument: the bird is a flute and the duck is an oboe.
The conductor leads with a baton.
check: In "Peter and the Wolf", the bird is a...
Where do strings sit in an orchestra?
What does a conductor lead with?
lessons.try: Listen to a part of "Peter and the Wolf". Can you name the duck's instrument?

learn: Repetition is when music repeats a part.
Contrast is when music changes to something new.
Good music balances repetition and contrast.
lessons.try: Listen to a song and say "same" or "different" at each new part.

learn: AB form has two parts. ABA has a part, a new part, then the first part again.
Rondo form keeps coming back to A: A B A C A.
Labelling form helps you understand music.
check: First part, new part, first part again
A B A C A is...
lessons.try: Make an ABA dance: walk, hop, walk.

learn: A phrase is a musical sentence.
Phrases can be the same, similar or different.
Singers breathe at the end of a phrase.
check: At the end of a phrase
In the middle of a word
lessons.try: Sing "Twinkle, Twinkle" and draw an arc in the air for each phrase.

learn: Program music tells a story or paints a picture without words.
Saint-Saëns' "The Carnival of the Animals" (1886) uses music to show a lion, a swan, an elephant and more.
The elephant is played by a low, heavy double bass.
check: Music that tells a story without words
Who wrote "The Carnival of the Animals"?
lessons.try: Listen to "The Elephant" from "The Carnival of the Animals" and move like it.

learn: Musicians can make sounds that remind us of things: rain, thunder, footsteps.
Fast, high notes might be a bird. Slow, low notes might be a bear.
Rattles can sound like rain.
check: Fast, high notes might sound like a...
Slow, low notes might be a...
lessons.try: Make a rainstorm with your hands: rub, snap, pat, stomp, then back down.

learn: You can create music to tell a story.
Choose an instrument or sound for each character.
Play their sounds when they appear in the story.
check: In a sound story, each character gets...
When do you play a character's sound?
lessons.try: Tell "The Three Billy Goats Gruff" with a sound for each goat and the troll.

learn: Folk songs are traditional songs passed down by people over many years.
"Oh! Susanna" by Stephen Foster (1848) became a popular American folk song.
Folk songs often tell about work, journeys and everyday life.
lessons.try: Learn a folk song from a family member.

learn: Latin American music often uses lively rhythms and instruments like maracas, guitars and claves.
Mariachi bands from Mexico include violins, trumpets and guitars.
Many songs are for dancing and celebrations.
check: Which instrument is in mariachi bands?
lessons.try: Shake a homemade maraca to a lively song.

learn: In Japan, the koto is a long string instrument plucked on the floor.
In Indonesia, a gamelan is a group of gongs and metal xylophones.
In West Africa, drumming groups play interlocking rhythms, and a talking drum can copy speech.
check: What can a talking drum copy?
lessons.try: Play a simple interlocking rhythm with a partner: you clap 1 and 3, they clap 2 and 4.

learn: Improvising means making up music on the spot.
You can improvise a rhythm, a melody or words.
Using the pentatonic notes (do, re, mi, sol, la) always sounds good together.
check: Making up music on the spot
lessons.try: Improvise a four-beat rhythm and have someone echo it.

learn: Composing means creating music and writing it down.
Start with a short rhythm, then add pitches.
You can write your music with notes or with your own symbols.
check: Can you use your own symbols?
lessons.try: Compose a four-measure song and write it down.

learn: Performers practise until they feel ready.
On stage, stand tall, look at the audience and smile.
If you make a mistake, keep going. Bow at the end when people clap.
check: What do performers do before a show?
If you make a mistake, you...
What do you do when people clap?
lessons.try: Perform your song for your family and take a bow.
